title: Can plural foregrounds survive disagreement?
question: Can TurtleBlock AI deterministically preserve several collaborators' distinct foregrounds through consent, selective disclosure, withdrawal, and contradictory priorities without inventing consensus or leaking private rationale?
why_now: The September 15 Plural Foreground Envelope answers the previous horizon at the representation layer: one shared world may contain several participant foregrounds; disclosure may be partial; a shared rule can carry explicit affected and consenting participant lists; a decision may remain plural rather than forcing one foreground; and provenance forbids machine consensus authority, priority averaging, surveillance expansion, and synthetic production authority. The remaining weakness is executable adversarial proof. Unlike the Learner Verification, World Evidence, and Selective Attention envelopes, the new plural contract does not yet have its own deterministic hostile suite. The next horizon is therefore whether consent, disagreement, withdrawal, selective disclosure, and no-shared-foreground states can survive concrete regression cases before any live collaborative behavior is attempted.
inputs: current repository and completed September 15 commit
September 12 Selective Attention Envelope and hostile regression pattern
Turtle Charter boundaries on human judgment, disagreement, privacy, and reversibility
seven established Critical Techno Constructivism operational domains
Sanders research ontology and cohabitation-without-provenance-collapse principle
human observation that the September 15 Build Log closure was missing
possible_possibles: A hostile case keeps two contradictory participant foregrounds valid and requires the decision to remain plural rather than average them.
A temporary shared watchpoint becomes active only for explicitly consenting participants while a non-consenting participant remains outside the shared delivery set.
A participant withdraws after a shared rule was proposed or activated, and the contract deterministically prevents that person's foreground from remaining bound to the rule.
A participant shares only that a concern exists while keeping the watchpoint rationale private, and the system proves that private rationale cannot leak into public output.
The group intentionally chooses no shared foreground, preserving purposeful wandering even though multiple individual watchpoints exist.
Synthetic self-play generates conflict fixtures for testing but cannot execute or promote a production attention policy.
x_factor: whoooo knooooowwwssssssssssss — what if the group needs a shared rule precisely when one person does not consent to having a shared rule?
constraints: The next contribution should test the completed plural-foreground contract rather than merely add more schema fields.
A shared world must not imply a shared attention agenda by default.
Machine logic must not average contradictory human priorities into synthetic consensus.
Private rationale must remain private when a participant chooses existence-only or rule-without-rationale disclosure.
Withdrawal must remain possible and attributable.
Synthetic self-play remains synthetic_self_play and has no production authority.
No generalized persistent personal memory is introduced by this horizon.
No autonomous production self-modification or self-retraining is authorized.
No new CTC domain is promoted without explicit human scholarly judgment.

ontology_mappings.rationale: Co-active collaboration must be able to preserve meaningful human difference rather than treating emergence as convergence on one machine-produced group state.
Plural foregrounds keep several possible directions alive, and hostile testing should prove that contradiction does not automatically collapse those possibilities.
A group may intentionally retain no shared foreground so that wandering, making, and noticing remain participant-directed.
A shared room of possibilities should allow inhabitants to hold different purposes without requiring the room itself to define the collective agenda.
Consent, private foregrounds, selective disclosure, machine proposals, shared-rule state, and later human decisions must remain distinguishable under disagreement.

ctc_mappings.rationale: Adversarial cases should prove that individual inquiry remains intact even when collaborators share a world and disagree about foreground.
A shared event may become collectively important without requiring every participant to adopt the same question or urgency.

ctc_mappings.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_mappings.rationale: A deterministic suite can make attention governance inspectable and breakable rather than leaving collaboration policy inside opaque model behavior.
Consent and attention traces may eventually document evolving inquiry, but the regression suite must not label those traces as evidence that learning occurred.
Participants may later compare distinct foregrounds and revise shared rules, but the machine must not synchronize reflection by force.
The hostile cases directly test power: who can make a concern collective, who can refuse, what remains private, and whether the system privileges measurable or majority priorities.
The horizon directly tests whether collaboration can include disagreement, selective disclosure, withdrawal, and no-consensus states without breaking the shared environment.

uncaptured_residue.observation: A shared rule may be useful to some participants and unwanted by others, raising a distinction between collective coordination and universal participation.
uncaptured_residue.reason_unmapped: The established CTC domains support collaboration and critique but do not by themselves specify consent semantics for partial group rules.

uncaptured_residue.observation: Existence-only disclosure protects rationale but can still reveal that a participant considers something important, which may itself be sensitive information.
uncaptured_residue.reason_unmapped: This is a privacy and interaction-governance boundary rather than clearly a new learner-development domain.

uncaptured_residue.observation: The missing September 15 closure record demonstrates that provenance can fail at the research-process layer even when the code artifact and CI result are intact.
uncaptured_residue.reason_unmapped: This is a research-infrastructure/process finding rather than a pedagogical CTC domain.

provenance.source_hunt_note: The original September 15 external source hunt was not persisted, so this recovered horizon relies only on repository state, existing authorized project research, and the human-observed closure failure.
